title: Analysis of CNS-Associated Lymphatics
protocol: Anesthetize mouse by injection of a suitable dosage of anesthesia.
Make an incision through the abdominal wall and cut both sides of the rib cage to expose the heart.
Clip the right auricle with a small scissor.
Perfuse the mouse through the left ventricle with ~15 ml of ice-cold PBS containing 5 U/ml heparin at a rate of ~10 ml per minute until the liver is clear of blood.
Replace the PBS-containing syringe with the PFA-containing syringe and perfuse manually with ~15 ml of 4% PFA at a rate of ~10 ml/min.
Remove the skin from the back and head of the dorsal site of the mouse with a pair of blunt scissors.
Decapitate mouse close to the skull, approximately at C1 level.
Make a transverse cut through the L5 vertebrae, just above the hips.
Continue with a longitudinal incision from the anterior end down the right side of the spinal cord until reaching the cervical region.
Repeat longitudinal cut along the left side of the spinal cord.
Lift the column and separate it from muscles, organs and connective tissue underneath.
Keep the skull and spinal cord in 4% PFA at 4°C for 24 hours.
Fill a petri dish with PBS and place the spinal cord ventral side up.
Clip neural arch bilaterally one to two segments at a time using angled spring scissors.
Lift the end of the loose bone and cut across the neural spine to remove bone and expose the ventral surface of the spinal cord.
Hold edges of the spinal column on either side with two straight forceps and crack open carefully.
Remove spinal cord and adherent meninges in one piece and place in petri dish with fresh PBS.
Use spring microscissors to make a midline incision of the meninges along the ventral surface of the spinal cord.
Remove meninges and place in 24-well plate with 1 ml PBS.
Remove muscles caudal of the skull.

Make two incisions: one starting at the brainstem and going counterclockwise toward the olfactory bulb, and another in clockwise direction on the left side of the head until reaching the rostral part.
Use forceps to pick up the bone at the inferior end and bend it over without damaging the attached dura mater.
Place the skullcap in 24-well plate with 1 ml of 4% PFA and incubate for at least 2 hours at room temperature or overnight at 4°C.
Wash once with 1 ml PBS.

Carefully remove meninges (dura and some arachnoid) from interior part of the skull cap using fine forceps under a dissecting scope, starting at the top and pulling down in the middle part before removing the sides.
Place dissected meninges in 1 ml of PBS in a 24-well plate.
Wash tissue once in 0.5 ml PBS and incubate in 0.3 ml blocking solution for 1 hour at room temperature.
Immunostain the meninges with 0.3 ml primary antibody, such as VEGFR-3, Lyve-1 and podoplanin (at a concentration of 1:100, 1:400, and 1:100) in PBST overnight at 4°C.
Decant the solution and wash with 0.5 ml PBS for 5 minutes at room temperature. Repeat two times with fresh PBS.
Incubate the tissue with 0.3 ml secondary antibody conjugated with fluorescent protein (at a concentration of 1–2 μg/ml) in PBST with 1% BSA for 1 hour at room temperature in the dark.
Decant the secondary antibody solution.
Wash once with PBS.
Incubate in 0.3 ml Hoechst or DAPI at a concentration of 0.1–1 μg/ml in PBS for 3 min at room temperature in the dark.
Rinse twice with 0.5 ml PBS.
Transfer meninges to a glass slide with a few drops of PBS using paintbrushes.
Unfold meninges carefully and aspirate PBS to flatten them, letting them dry.
Cover flattened meninges with mounting medium to preserve fluorescence.
Seal the cover with nail polish to prevent movement, avoiding any bubbles.
The tissue is now ready for imaging using a conventional widefield microscope, confocal microscope, or an ultramicroscope.
Transfer meninges from brain (or spinal cord) into a 2 ml tube containing 0.5 ml RPMI.
Add 0.5 ml of 2× enzymatic cocktail and incubate the tube in a 37°C incubator on a rotating mixer for 15 minutes.
Filter the resulting single-cell suspension through a 70 μm cell strainer into a 50 ml tube, adding 20 ml of ice-cold PBS to wash the strainer.
Centrifuge cells for 10 minutes at 320 × g at 4°C and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend each pellet in 200 μl of ice-cold sorting buffer and count total number using an automated cell counter or hemacytometer.
Place cells in a 96-well plate.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 min at 320 × g and 4 °C.
Add 100 μl of primary antibody cocktail and resuspend with pipette.
Incubate the mixture for 30 min on ice.
Add 10 μl of DAPI (10 μg/ml) to the cells.
Incubate the cells for 5 min on ice.
Centrifuge the cells for 5 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant and wash the cells with 100 μl sorting buffer.
Repeat the previous step of washing the cells.
Keep cell samples on ice until they are ready for sorting or analyzing on a flow cytometer.
Anesthetize mice by intraperitoneal injection of 100 mg/kg Ketamine and 10 mg/kg Xylazine.
Maintain body temperature at 37°C during anesthesia.
Shave the neck area of the mouse.
Place the mouse on a stereotaxic frame and secure with tooth and ear bars.
Swab the surgical site with 10% iodine, followed by 70% ethanol.
Make a 1 cm sagittal incision over the occipital bone and cervical spinal cord.
Separate muscle layers using blunt dissection with forceps.
Hold muscles apart with retractors.
Lower the mouse's body by ~1 cm to form a 140° angle head position.
Expose the posterior atlantooccipital membrane.
Penetrate the posterior atlantooccipital membrane with a Hamilton syringe equipped with a bevel-ended 33-G needle.
Dilute 2 μl of tracer in artificial cerebrospinal fluid.
Slowly infuse diluted tracer intra cisternally.
Hold the needle in place for approximately 2 minutes.
Remove the needle slowly while observing for backflow.
After injection, remove retractors and suture skin.
Monitor mouse until recovery.
Two hours after tracer injection, perfuse mice with cold saline.
Perfuse mice with 4% PFA.
Harvest CSF-draining lymph nodes (deep and superficial cervical) into 4% PFA.
Wash tissue with PBS.
Place lymph nodes in 30% sucrose overnight at 4°C or until sunk to the bottom of the tube.
Place lymph nodes in a mold with OCT and freeze on dry ice.
Cut 30 μm sections from lymph nodes using a cryostat.
Collect sections onto gelatin-coated glass slides.
Draw a border around the sectioned tissue with a hydrophobic pen.
Let the bordered tissue air-dry for a few minutes at room temperature.
Rinse the tissue in PBS and then wash with PBST for 3 min at room temperature.
Incubate with 200–250 μl of blocking solution in PBST for 20 min at room temperature in a humidifying chamber, then wash once with PBST for 3 min at room temperature.
Add 200–250 μl antibody cocktail in PBST with 0.5% BSA and incubate for 1 h at room temperature or overnight at 4 °C in a humidifying chamber.
Wash the tissue with PBS for 5 min at room temperature, repeat wash twice.
Add 200–250 μl of secondary antibody mix in PBST with 1% BSA and incubate for 1 h at room temperature in a humidifying chamber.
Wash the tissue once with PBS for 5 min at room temperature.
Add 200–250 μl DAPI or Hoechst solution and incubate for 5 min at room temperature in a humidifying chamber.
Wash the tissue twice with PBS for 5 min at room temperature.
Let the slides air-dry, then add mounting medium plus glass coverslip and seal with nail polish.
Quantify tracer amounts by total counts in draining versus nondraining lymph nodes.
Measure area covered by peptides or other smaller tracers in lymph nodes.
Collect deep cervical lymph nodes two hours after injection of fluorescently labeled ovalbumin into the cisterna magna.
Immunostain collected lymph node sections for imaging.
